hints: Follow the reaction sequence step by step, first ask what type of compound lithium aluminium hydride makes from a carboxylic acid.
Propanoic acid is reduced to propan-1-ol, then think about what happens when an alcohol reacts with a carboxylic acid in concentrated sulfuric acid.
Identify the functional group in X and recall which two large scale uses are famous for that family of compounds.
walkthrough:
**Reduce the acid to an alcohol**

Lithium aluminium hydride is a very strong reducing agent. It reduces a carboxylic acid all the way to a primary alcohol.

Chemical change:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow[\text{excess}]{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$
So the organic product is propan-1-ol.

**Esterify to make product X**

An alcohol plus a carboxylic acid with concentrated sulfuric acid gives an ester by condensation, with water lost. Sulfuric acid acts as catalyst and dehydrating agent.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So X is propyl ethanoate, an ester.

**Recall commercial uses of esters**

Esters are volatile, sweet smelling liquids. They dissolve many organic compounds, so they are widely used as solvents in glues, paints and inks.

They also have fruity smells and tastes, so they are widely used as flavourings and perfumes. They are not used as fuels, that is a major use of alcohols such as ethanol. Therefore statements 2 and 3 are correct, but 1 is not.

options.A: Incorrect. This option means 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. While X, propyl ethanoate, is used as a solvent and flavouring, it is not a major fuel. Students choosing this may correctly identify X as useful but confuse esters with alcohols like ethanol which are used as biofuels.
options.B: Incorrect. This option means 1 and 2 only are correct. It correctly includes solvent but wrongly includes fuel and wrongly leaves out flavouring. Esters are famous for fruity odours, so flavouring is a key use.
options.C: Correct. This option means 2 and 3 only are correct. X is propyl ethanoate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$), an ester. Esters are major commercial solvents and are widely used as artificial flavourings and fragrances because of their sweet, fruity smells.
options.D: Incorrect. This option means 1 only is correct. Fuel is the one use that does NOT apply to X. This would be chosen if you mistook the reduction product propan-1-ol for the final product, since alcohols can be fuels, and missed the second esterification step.
